description: Fig. 7 is a single-panel conceptual schematic (not a data plot) illustrating how the tensile elongation of austenitic steels varies with temperature, reproduced from reference [32]. The vertical axis is labelled "Tensile Elongation" with an upward-pointing arrow and carries no numeric scale; the horizontal axis has no label, ticks or values, and represents temperature increasing to the right. A long horizontal arrow above the frame points leftward and is labelled "Enhanced glide planarity", so the left side corresponds to low temperature / low SFE and the right side to high temperature. Two dashed vertical lines divide the panel into three regimes marked I (right), II (centre) and III (left). Region III is annotated "DIMT", region II "Planar glide except DIMT", region I "Wavy glide". The solid curve starts low at the far left, rises steeply through region III, peaks at the III/II dashed boundary, then decreases monotonically across region II, drops steeply and flattens into a low plateau in region I. The figure therefore argues that maximum tensile elongation occurs in the DIMT-to-planar-glide transition at intermediate temperature, whereas both fully wavy glide and DIMT-dominated behaviour reduce elongation. No numerical values appear anywhere in the panel. The whole group is a single schematic, with no micrographs, spectra or measured data.
measured_quantities: tensile elongation (arbitrary/conceptual scale; no unit or value printed)
deformation temperature (implied horizontal axis; no values, ticks or units printed)

observations.observation: The vertical axis is labelled 'Tensile Elongation' with an upward-pointing arrow and shows no numeric scale or tick values.
The horizontal axis of the panel carries no axis title, no ticks and no values; its physical meaning (temperature) is supplied only by the caption.
A horizontal arrow drawn above the plot frame points to the left and is labelled 'Enhanced glide planarity', so glide planarity increases leftwards (towards lower temperature).
Two dashed vertical lines divide the panel into three regions labelled I on the right, II in the centre and III on the left.
Region III is annotated with the text 'DIMT'.
Region II is annotated with the text 'Planar glide except DIMT'.
Region I is annotated with the text 'Wavy glide'.

The solid elongation curve is low at the far left, rises steeply through region III, reaches its maximum exactly at the dashed line separating regions III and II, then falls monotonically across region II and flattens to a low plateau in region I.
No numerical values for elongation, temperature or SFE are printed anywhere in the panel; all trends are qualitative.

The caption states the figure is an 'Illustration for the temperature dependence of tensile elongation of austenitic steels [32]', i.e. it is a reproduced/adapted schematic rather than new data from this study.
The caption assigns the horizontal direction of the figure to temperature, which the panel itself does not label or quantify.

The figure links three deformation regimes (wavy glide, planar glide except DIMT, DIMT) to the magnitude of tensile elongation, implying the maximum elongation lies in the intermediate, planar-glide-dominated regime.

subfigures.description: Schematic line plot of tensile elongation (y-axis, upward arrow, no scale) versus an unlabelled temperature axis (no ticks) for austenitic steels. A top arrow directed leftward reads 'Enhanced glide planarity'. Two dashed vertical lines split the plot into zones III (left, labelled 'DIMT'), II (centre, labelled 'Planar glide except DIMT') and I (right, labelled 'Wavy glide'). The curve rises from the left, peaks at the III/II boundary, then falls through II and levels off low in I.
